tldr: Disclosure up front: the reviewer works in Growth and Marketing at Heyy, so treat the scores here as informed but not neutral — Intercom's numbers are backed by thousands of independent reviews; Heyy's aren't yet.

Heyy is built around an 'AI Employee' model — one agent configured with identity, knowledge, permissioned CRM read/write access, and explicit exit-point logic, deployed across WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, Live Chat, and SMS from one workspace.

Intercom centers on the Fin AI agent layered over a mature shared inbox, help center, and ticketing system, with phone support and a large independent review base (2,900+ on G2 alone) that Heyy doesn't have yet.

Pricing is the clearest gap: Intercom publishes seat pricing ($29+/seat/mo) plus a $0.99-per-resolution AI fee; Heyy's plan tiers are documented by feature limits, not dollar figures, so you'll need to contact sales to compare real cost.

If you need phone support or a vendor with a long, independently-verifiable track record, Intercom is the lower-risk pick today. If you want granular control over what an AI agent can read/write in your CRM and you're comfortable being an early adopter, Heyy is worth a Playground test.

Run the actual math you can run: Intercom's $29/seat Essential tier plus $0.99/resolution is at least a knowable number you can forecast against expected volume; Heyy's Hobby/Pro/Ultra tiers are documented only by feature limits (1 AI Employee/3MB knowledge on Hobby, up to 3 employees/50MB on Ultra), so you can't build a real cost model here until you've talked to sales.

featureMatrix.toolB: Contact data available, less granular permissioning documented

verdict: There's a real conflict of interest to flag here rather than bury: I work in Growth and Marketing at Heyy, so I'm not an outside, disinterested reviewer on this one. Here's what I can say honestly regardless — the attribute-permission model (Read, Share, Update, with Update requiring Read first) is a more deliberate design for avoiding bad CRM writes than anything documented in Intercom's own docs, and the explicit warning against crawling live store data for prices is the kind of specific guidance you only write after you've watched it go wrong for a real customer. But Intercom has 2,900+ reviews behind its numbers and Heyy has zero — that's not a small gap, it's the entire reason review aggregators like G2 exist, and no amount of thoughtful product design substitutes for that track record yet. The pricing situation makes the comparison even more lopsided in practice: Intercom's $29/seat plus $0.99/resolution is a number you can build a budget model around today, while Heyy's tiers are documented only in feature limits — you genuinely can't compare total cost of ownership here until you've had a sales conversation, which is a real disadvantage if you're trying to comparison-shop before committing time to a demo. If you need a proven vendor today, especially one with phone support, Intercom is the lower-risk pick and it isn't close. If you're an early-adopter type who wants tighter control over what an AI agent can touch in your CRM and you're willing to run the Playground yourself and get real pricing before deciding, Heyy is worth thirty minutes of your time — just go in knowing you're evaluating a newer product on its design, not its track record.
